original_source_text: In fault-tolerant quantum circuit synthesis, T gates supplied via magic states dominate space–time cost, while Clifford gates incur negligible overhead. Conventional flows minimize AND count in an {XOR, AND, NOT} basis as a proxy for T, which neglects phase cancellation and can be far from T-optimal. We instead formulate an exact T synthesis problem and canonicalize Boolean functions under Clifford equivalence. By precomputing T-optimal implementations up to seven variables and developing a specialized mapper, we reduce the T count by up to 16% on EPFL benchmarks and improve the best-known T counts of several cryptographic modules.

record_under_review.limits: The public description does not enumerate all circuits, runtime costs, or the scalability boundary of exact precomputation.
record_under_review.method_or_artifact: Exact T-synthesis formulation with Clifford-equivalence canonicalization, precomputed small-function libraries, and a specialized mapper.

record_under_review.problem: AND-count minimization is an imperfect proxy for T cost in fault-tolerant quantum synthesis because it misses phase cancellation.

conditions.finding: Six EPFL arithmetic circuits; comparison against exact-MC mapping; customized mapper reports 5.3 percent geomean T-count reduction.
Library-only substitution reports about 0.5 percent geomean reduction and regressions on some circuits.
Exact solver bound is N <= 7 total qubits, not seven arbitrary logical inputs; larger instances use suboptimal solutions.
Correctness assumes clean output ancilla initialized to zero; not unrestricted unitary equivalence.
Mapping stages account for at most 11.7 percent of total synthesis runtime in the reported QLUT evaluation.
